title: Cellular composition and epithelial cell state contribute in opposite directions to the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma transcriptome - reproducibility package
description:
Reproducible analysis code and derived intermediate results for a study that re-attributes the transcriptomic shift along the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence to epithelial-intrinsic versus stromal-compositional components.

The package contains no new primary data. Every script operates on public datasets from NCBI GEO (GSE41258, GSE37364, GSE20916, GSE41657, GSE4183, GSE117606, GSE15960, GSE161277, GSE109308, GSE128435, GSE303070, GSE8671) and on derived tables written by earlier stages, so that every number, table and figure in the manuscript can be traced back to a script and an input file.

Stages: A consensus signature (Stouffer integration across discovery cohorts) - B drift diagnostics - C LCM-based compartment attribution - D three-layer pattern matrix - E sensitivity analysis - F single-cell P x U decomposition - G supplementary-table build - H figure rendering - I manuscript artefact assembly - J robustness and sensitivity analyses.

The five CSV products of the upstream R pipeline (limma / WGCNA) are shipped under upstream_r/ so that the Python package is self-contained. See REPRODUCIBILITY.md for the full script-to-artefact mapping, and README.md for the environment and quick-start instructions. Released under the MIT License.

v1.0.5 aligns the archive with the revised manuscript and deposits the robustness and sensitivity analyses that the revised Methods section reports. Nine new scripts (bootstrap confidence intervals, sample-level label permutation, module-block sign-flip with variance-inflation control, doublet and SVA sensitivity, leave-one-cohort-out stability, an independent validation on GSE8671, and an arithmetic simulation of the drift-correction step) ship with their archived JSON outputs and two robustness figures. The supplementary-table file names now carry the manuscript's re-labelled table numbers (Table S3 = single-cell a/b, S4 = four-cohort performance, S5 = three-layer pattern a/b); cell content is byte-identical to v1.0.4. No reported number changed value except as documented in the manuscript revision.

v1.0.4 brings the record title and the shipped code into line with the submitted manuscript. The title now matches the manuscript, so that the DOI printed in the Code availability statement resolves to a record describing the same study. Three things changed in the code. _bmc_references.json now carries all 31 references, and every one of the 11 GEO series is accompanied by the publication that first described it; verify_bmc.py grew from 24 to 31 checks, one of which requires that citation at the first mention of each accession. make_figs.py no longer folds the panel heat map to max(AUC, 1 − AUC): a panel that separates the stages in the opposite direction now reads below 0.5 instead of as its mirror image, which is what the figure legend asks the reader to look for. build_bmc_manuscript.py and qa_numbers.py follow the undirected scoring convention defined in the Methods, and record the directed variant alongside it. The heat map is the only figure whose appearance changed; no other reported number, table or figure differs from v1.0.3.

v1.0.3 fixes one line: the README archived-version row had a doubled https://doi.org/ prefix and named the previous release. It now points at the concept DOI, which always resolves to the newest version.

Changes in v1.0.2 (reproducibility audit; no reported number, table or figure changed). Two scripts no longer resolve their working directory from a developer-local absolute path. Inputs that earlier stages read but that had never been shipped are now included: consensus_signature_tier.csv, manuscript_facts.py, epithelial_core_genes.json, stromal_layer_genes.json, cohort_hunt2.py, gpl_soft_map.py and collide_results.json. The classifier module matters most: without it the sample classifier silently degraded to substring matching, which merged one cohort's carcinoma group into other and wrote truncated results with exit code 0. three_layer_check.py now refuses to overwrite archived results when a cohort was skipped (it writes *.partial.json and exits 2), and drift_diag.json is regenerated under the shipped code. REQUIREMENTS.txt pins Pillow and states explicitly that figure bytes additionally depend on the FreeType build that Matplotlib links against, which no pip pin can control. REPRODUCIBILITY.md section 9 gives the data-preparation order, the working route for the one platform whose annotation is absent from GEO, and exactly which artefacts are byte-identical and which are only semantically identical.

The development version of this package is maintained at github.com/Yao204-116/crc-adenoma-carcinoma-compartment-attribution.
